articles.title: ‘Partly the movie’s fault I’m a writer at all’: why Wonder Boys is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers picking their most comforting rewatches is a tribute to Curtis Hanson’s insightful 2000 comedy drama I’m allergic to movies and books about writers. Washed-up novelists, aspiring screenwriters, creative writing professors in the throes of a midlife crisis who cheat on their wives – take your pick. Chalk it up to my being a writer who for two decades wrote continually and fruitlessly about writers. And yet, I love Wonder Boys, Curtis Hanson’s 2000 comedy drama about a rumpled creative writing professor who can’t seem to finish his second novel and is having an affair with his boss’s wife. It’s partly the movie’s fault I’m a writer at all. articles.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
articles.summary: She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. articles.title: The DCU’s James Gunn and Peter Safran are out – this is the biggest disaster to hit superhero movies in years
articles.summary: The adventurous weirdness of the Gunn/Safran era that fans responded to is now history. Can the DCU ever get back on track? What was Warner Bros’ plan in 2022 , when the studio decided to reboot its superhero output, jettison the increasingly muddled DC Extended Universe (DCEU) and replace it with a sparkling new DC Universe (DCU)? In part it was to wipe the slate clean after years of false starts, abandoned storylines and tonal lurches. There was a little bit of Marvel envy to proceedings, and quite possibly a desire to avoid having to ever again discuss Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice’s numerous failings . But mostly it was to take advantage of hiring of a man whom nobody could accuse of being short of ideas on how to make comic book movies. To a greater or lesser extent, the plan was James Gunn.
